note_on_duplicates: Concepts 001-012 each have two folder variants: underscore-separated (e.g., 001_parallel_bit_stream_structural_indexing) and hyphen-separated (e.g., 001_parallel-bit-stream-structural-indexing). Both variants contain concept.json and README.md; the underscore variants additionally contain literature.json. Concepts 013 and 014 have only underscore-variant folders. The index.json canonical paths reference hyphen variants for 001-012 and underscore variants for 013-014. Total physical folders: 26 (12 pairs + 2 singletons = 14 unique concepts).

missing_links.rationale: Concept 005 (vectorized classification) produces per-category bitmasks including the quote bitmask, which is the direct input to concept 002 (CLMUL quote pairing). The classification-to-quote-pairing pipeline is the core Phase 1 dataflow, yet adjacency.json has no edge from 005 to 002.

Concept 003 (row-length prediction) and concept 008 (field-width prediction) are closely coupled — row-length is the sum of field widths. The reverse edge (008 -> 003) exists, but the forward edge (003 -> 008) is missing. Row-length prediction residuals could inform field-width entropy estimation.

Concept 005 (classification) outputs character class labels that feed directly into concept 007 (branchless FSM). The FSM's (state, character_class) lookup table consumes classification output. No edge exists between them in adjacency.json.

Concept 013 (speculative execution) checkpoints parser state before speculative Phase 2 work and rolls back on misprediction. This directly depends on the two-phase split (concept 010). Concept 014 has this edge, but 013 does not.
Concept 014 (optimistic parsing) relies on chunk-boundary validation that uses quote-parity resolution (concept 002) to detect mid-quoted-field splits. No edge exists from 014 to 002.

Concept 009 (UTF-8 validation fusion) fuses validation into the same PSHUFB pipeline used by concept 005 (character classification). They share the same SIMD instruction stream. The reverse edge (005 -> 009 via 001) exists indirectly, but no direct edge from 009 to 005.

blind_spot_concepts.name: SIMD-aware memory allocator
blind_spot_concepts.rationale: Experiments show allocation reduction ranges 6.9x (utf8_heavy) to 200x (wide_table), but per-byte throughput still varies 3.3x across datasets (1127-3682 MB/s). Phase 2 consumes 31.2% of total time and is bottlenecked by pointer-chasing in structural index arrays. A SIMD-width-aligned arena allocator that pre-allocates field output buffers at 32/64-byte boundaries would eliminate per-field allocation overhead, reduce L1d miss rate from cross-buffer writes, and allow Phase 2 field extraction to use aligned SIMD stores (VMOVDQA) instead of unaligned stores.
blind_spot_concepts.evidence: speculation_analysis.json shows alloc_reduction_factor varies 6.9-200x; hardware_counters.json shows Phase 2 at 31.2% of total time with L1d miss rate 1.5% driven by dual-pointer access pattern

blind_spot_concepts.name: Structural density adaptive dispatch
blind_spot_concepts.rationale: Throughput correlates r=-0.82 with structural character density: simple_uniform (high delimiter density, ~1 structural char per 7.8 bytes) achieves 1234 MB/s, while embedded_newlines (low density, ~1 per 73 bytes) achieves 3682 MB/s. Dynamically switching between a dense extraction algorithm (bitmask iteration with TZCNT loop for high-density blocks) and a sparse extraction algorithm (memchr-style SIMD seeking for low-density blocks) based on popcount of the structural bitmask per 64-byte block could optimize across all dataset types. The dispatch decision is a single POPCNT instruction per block.
blind_spot_concepts.evidence: throughput_matrix.json shows 3x throughput range across datasets; embedded_newlines (sparse structure) is 3x faster than simple_uniform (dense structure) despite similar SIMD Phase 1 costs, indicating Phase 2 extraction strategy should adapt to structural density
